summary: Bhutan's Department of Immigration says nationals of all countries other than India must obtain a visa before entry, applied for at immi.gov.bt or through Bhutanese tourism service providers; nationals of Bangladesh and the Maldives are eligible for a visa on arrival, and Indian nationals for an entry permit on arrival. The visa fee is US$40 per person. Visitors other than those from India pay a Sustainable Development Fee of USD 200 per person per night, with a 50% discount to USD 100 for US-dollar-paying tourists valid until 31 August 2027; for guests from India it is 1,200 Indian rupees per person per night.

fee.notes: Visa fee, non-refundable and non-transferable, paid with the application. The Sustainable Development Fee is charged separately for each night: Bhutan's Department of Immigration says it is USD 200 per person per night, with a 50% discount to USD 100 for US-dollar-paying tourists valid until 31 August 2027; children aged 6 to 11 get a 50% discount and children under 6 pay nothing.

fee.text: The visa fee is US$40 per person; this fee is non-refundable and non-transferable.

processing.text: Turnaround time is 03 working days from the receipt of the complete application including the payment of applicable fee

extendable.text: Yes, guests can extend their stay via the online visa/permit application portal on the same site, using the same log-in details that were used to process the original visa/permit.

name.text: Nationals of Bangladesh and the Maldives are eligible for visa on arrival.

method.text: Visitors from Bangladesh and the Maldives also require a visa, but this can be applied for and approved either in advance of travel or upon arrival in Bhutan.

fee.text: There is a one-off fee of US$40 for the processing of your application.

stayDays.text: The visa allows you to remain in Bhutan for a maximum of 90 days from the date of entry.

extendable.text: Yes, provided the extension is applied for before the original visa or permit expires.

passportValidity.text: Bhutan's Immigration Rules and Regulations 2023 say the passport shall be valid for at least six months from the intended date of departure from the Kingdom. The Department of Immigration says Indian nationals may produce a passport or a Voter Identity Card in original at the port of entry.

travelInsurance.text: Not required. Bhutan's Department of Tourism says the requirement for mandatory travel insurance was lifted on April 23, 2024, but strongly recommends that all guests have travel insurance before visiting.

onwardTicket.text: No official source we could read states an onward-ticket requirement for visitors to Bhutan; Bhutan's Immigration Rules and Regulations 2023 list none among the conditions of entry.

source.name: Department of Immigration, Bhutan — Immigration Rules and Regulations of the Kingdom of Bhutan 2023 (conditions of entry: no onward-ticket requirement)

proofOfFunds.text: Bhutan's Immigration Rules and Regulations 2023 say a foreigner seeking entry shall prove adequate means to support their stay in the Kingdom without recourse to public funds. No official source we could read states an amount.

source.name: Department of Immigration, Bhutan — Immigration Rules and Regulations of the Kingdom of Bhutan 2023
source.instrument: Immigration Rules and Regulations of the Kingdom of Bhutan 2023, rule 35

currencyLimits.text: Bhutan's Department of Tourism says you may bring cash equivalent to US$10,000 into the country. The UK government says foreign currency worth 10,000 US dollars or more taken into or out of Bhutan must be declared and cleared with the Royal Monetary Authority of Bhutan, and that up to 30,000 ngultrum can be taken in or out.

notes: The UK government says you can bring a small supply of tobacco for personal use but must pay taxes and duties and be able to show proof of payment if asked; Canada's travel advice says imported tobacco products for personal use are subject to a 200% tax.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Bhutan?
faq.answer: Yes, unless you are a national of India: Bhutan's Department of Immigration says Indian nationals need a permit, holding an Indian passport or Indian voter ID card. Nationals of Bangladesh and the Maldives are eligible for a visa on arrival, though the Department of Tourism recommends arranging it beforehand. Others obtain a visa before entry, applied for at immi.gov.bt or through Bhutanese tourism service providers, with a US$40 visa fee and the Sustainable Development Fee paid when the visa is processed. The Department of Immigration says foreigners can stay in the country as tourists for a maximum of 90 days.

faq.question: How much is Bhutan's Sustainable Development Fee?

faq.question: Do Indian citizens need a visa for Bhutan?

faq.question: Do I have to book a tour to visit Bhutan?

faq.question: How do I apply for a Bhutan visa?
faq.answer: Apply online at immi.gov.bt and pay the US$40 visa fee; the Sustainable Development Fee is paid at the time of processing the visa. faq.question: Can I extend my stay in Bhutan?

Bhutan's Department of Immigration says guests can extend their stay via the online visa/permit application portal, using the same log-in details, and must produce the original passport at the nearest immigration office; the extension fee and the SDF for the extended stay are paid through the same portal.
